context: A treemap dashboard with 5 color-coded divisions, ~100 product leaf cells each containing an embedded sparkline, and a 4-card KPI strip at the top summarizing total revenue, product count, top division, and growth leader.
first_impression: Dense but well-organized — the 5-division color structure acts as a strong visual anchor that prevents the 100-cell treemap from feeling chaotic.
what_works: The 5-color Tol palette (one per division) stays well under the 8-hue warning threshold and cleanly separates divisions at a glance; the KPI strip provides a scannable summary layer that offloads working memory before the viewer engages with the treemap detail.
what_doesnt: Smaller leaf cells render sparklines at ~10-15px height where line variation is imperceptible and the revenue label disappears entirely, reducing those cells to color patches with no data signal; the tooltip is the only way to recover full detail on small cells, but hover-gating information on a static-feeling dashboard creates a discoverability gap.
